name: Repo Review Skill
summary: Review a codebase for bugs, risks, missing tests, and integration issues.
description: Repo Review Skill is a reusable review protocol for agentic coding sessions. It changes the output from a vague summary into prioritized findings with file references, behavioral risk, missing tests, and verification gaps.
installSummary: This is a skill template, not a package install. Add the instruction file to the skill or rules mechanism supported by your agent, then test it against a small pull request before relying on it for larger reviews.

installSteps.title: Create the skill file
installSteps.body: Create a dedicated skill or rule file in your agent's instruction directory. Keep the skill narrowly focused on review behavior so it does not conflict with implementation tasks.
installSteps.code:
Name: Repo Review
Purpose: Find bugs, regressions, missing tests, security risks, and unclear behavior changes before merge.

installSteps.title: Define review output order
installSteps.body: Require findings first, ordered by severity, with file and line references. Summaries should come after findings, not before them.
installSteps.code: Output findings first. Each finding must include severity, file path, line number when available, concrete risk, and suggested fix direction.

installSteps.title: Add a verification rule
installSteps.body: The agent should state which tests were run or which tests are missing. If it cannot run tests, it should say so explicitly rather than implying confidence.

agentSetups.summary: Put this in a Codex skill or project instruction so review requests consistently use code-review mode.

steps.title: Project-level instruction
steps.body: Add the review behavior to AGENTS.md or the repo's chosen Codex instruction file when the whole project should use the same review standard.

steps.title: Review prompt
steps.body: Ask for review explicitly; do not mix review and implementation in the same request.
steps.code: Review this change for bugs, behavioral regressions, security risks, and missing tests. Findings first.

agentSetups.summary: Claude Code users can keep the skill text in CLAUDE.md or a reusable command/skill file depending on their setup.

steps.title: Add to CLAUDE.md
steps.body: For repo-specific standards, put the review protocol in CLAUDE.md. For reusable behavior, keep it as a command or skill template.

agentSetups.summary: Cursor users can adapt the same protocol as a project rule.

steps.title: Add Cursor rule
steps.body: Create a rule that applies when the user asks for code review, PR review, or risk analysis.

primaryUseCases: Audit a pull request for behavior regressions instead of style-only feedback.
Check whether a generated implementation actually satisfies the requested behavior.
Create a consistent review rubric for a small team using different coding agents.
highlights: Forces findings-first output so important issues are not buried.
Works across agents because it is instruction text rather than an agent-specific binary.
Pairs naturally with Playwright MCP for frontend verification and Context7 for library-specific review.
Makes missing tests and unverified assumptions visible.

configuration.title: Severity labels
configuration.body: Use a simple severity scale so reviews remain scannable.
configuration.code:
P0: blocks release
P1: likely bug or data/security risk
P2: important quality or test gap
P3: minor maintainability issue

configuration.title: Review scope
configuration.body: Tell the agent whether it should review only staged changes, the working tree, a branch diff, or a specific file list.

verificationSteps.title: Test on a known-bad diff
verificationSteps.body: Create or use a small diff with an obvious bug and confirm the skill reports the bug as a finding, not a vague note.

verificationSteps.title: Check line references
verificationSteps.body: The review should point to concrete files and lines when possible. If it cannot, it should explain why.

verificationSteps.title: Check test coverage language
verificationSteps.body: The final answer should say what was tested and what remains unverified.

troubleshooting.title: Review is too generic
troubleshooting.body: Tighten the trigger prompt and require concrete file references. Generic architectural commentary should be secondary.

troubleshooting.title: Agent starts fixing instead of reviewing
troubleshooting.body: Add a rule that review mode must not edit files unless the user explicitly asks for fixes.

securityNotes: Use this for security-sensitive diffs, but do not treat it as a replacement for dedicated security review.
Make sure private code stays inside the local agent environment approved by the team.
limitations: The skill improves review behavior but does not guarantee defect discovery.
Line references depend on whether the agent can inspect the exact diff.
Reviews are weaker when the repo has no tests or unclear expected behavior.
maintenanceNotes: Update the review rubric when the project adds new risk categories, frameworks, or testing conventions.
Keep the skill small; if it grows into many unrelated rules, split it into focused review skills.
